newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA SAYS BAKUN DAM LISTING COULD BE DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA SAYS BAKUN DAM LISTING COULD BE DELAYED.

text.p: Listing of Bakun Hydroelectric Corporation, Malaysia's biggest ever public offering, could be delayed by a dispute between its main contractors, Minister for Energy, Posts and Telecommunications Leo Moggie said on Monday.
"It might, it's a possibility," Moggie told reporters in reply to a question about Bakun's listing after addressing an energy conference.
"If the resolution of this (dispute) involves restructuring obviously they would have to look at the financing structure," the minister said.
The minister also said the dispute between Ekran Bhd and Asea Brown Boveri over a contract to build the $6.0 billion Bakun dam in Borneo state of Sarawak should be resolved in "the next month or so".
"I think time is approaching very fast," to keep the Bakun dam construction on schedule for its 2003 opening, he said.
He said Ekran and ABB had met on July 24 and were supposed to meet again within two weeks. He did not know if there had been a second meeting.
"Until we hear the final report (after the second meeting) we won't have a formal statement about what the resolutions will be," Moggie said.
He said there had been no statement from Ekran about the possibility of its pulling out of the project. "We have only heard a lot stories and rumours around about Ekran pulling out," he said.
The minister said the government would step in to mediate only if there was a deadlock.
"I would not want to say anything public that would jeopardise the discussion (between ABB and Ekran)," he said.
Bakun Hydroelectric Corporation Bhd, the operator of the dam, is planning an issue of 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit each. Ekran will hold 32 pecent of Bakun.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has hinted at the possibility of cancelling ABB's $5.5 billion contract if the dispute was not resolved.
The Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim had earlier said that the dispute was over "major terms" of the engineering, procurement and construction contract.
ABB is implementing the contract in consortium with Brazilian firm Companhia Brasileria Projectos Obras (CBPO).

ABB's portion of the work involves supplying six 420 mw hydro-generators, a 500-kv high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing a 650-km (400-mile) submarine cable to connect the dam to Peninsular Malaysia and civil works with CBPO.
